answers.question: How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks.
answers.answer:
You can run again about four days after the race, on Thu Oct 22, if stairs no longer make you wince and soreness is 2/10 or lower. If it isn't, walk again and try Saturday. Running on quads this sore tends to change your stride and drag recovery out.

The Thanksgiving 10K is realistic, so I wouldn't rule it out. Two easy weeks leave about three weeks of short, sharper work, and your marathon fitness carries over. A 10K needs sharpness more than extra mileage.

I'd rather you decide after a few easy miles than today. Tell me in your next check-in whether you want to race the 10K, take a longer break, or aim at something else. A friend wanting company is a good reason, but the real test is how your legs feel by Sun Nov 1.

new.analysis:
## Why the week looks like this

The marathon took a lot out of you, and the legs need days without impact. The race made up most of last week's effort: a relative effort of 369 out of 472, with 63% of the race in zone 4 at 86% of your max heart rate. That is why last week's easy-running share was only 33%. It was a race week, not a training problem. Your quads at 3/10 with stairs hard fit what that load does.

You followed last week's plan closely. Every run landed within a few hundred metres of the distance planned, you rested on both rest days, and you arrived at the start fresh. The taper did its job.

On the result, you were on pace through about 20 miles. Your first half averaged 8:32 a mile against the 8:35 that 3:45 needs. The back half slowed to 8:58, which cost roughly five minutes against your target. That is a common place for a second marathon to bite, and it points to what a future marathon block would work on. For now, take the 12-minute improvement and let the legs recover.

This week is about 9 miles against 41 last week, and all of it is easy. I put no strides and no long run in, because the point is to let the muscle damage settle before you load it again. The first run is a test, and walking is a fine answer if the test says not yet.

Next week, Oct 26 – Nov 1, should stay easy and build to about 12 to 16 miles over four or five short runs, still with no quality session. That is where we decide what comes next. If you pick the 10K, you would have three weeks of sharpening before it, with one quality session a week. If you want a longer break, we extend the easy running and aim at a spring goal instead.

safetyCallouts.title: Soreness should ease every day.
safetyCallouts.body: Quad and calf soreness at 3/10 after a marathon is common. If it gets worse after day three, turns sharp, or sits in one spot, stop running and see a physio or doctor.

safetyCallouts.title: Get a swollen calf checked.
safetyCallouts.body: If one calf becomes swollen, hot or painful at rest, see a doctor promptly. Have the blister looked at too if the toe turns red, hot or swollen.
